## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 – what to test next**
- Binary-search for the most realistic setting in which misbehaviour persists. 
  > "One way to think about our agentic misalignment work is as a single step in an ongoing binary search"  
  > -- `research__evhub_s_shortform_7f2bff4e` (2022-06-11; solo author)
- Remove spoonfeeding progressively. 
  > "the thing that we’re probably most excited about doing next is trying to remove that, to find situations where the model will pursue this deceptive instrumental alignment behavior and policy without starting with a lot of this spoon-feeding."  
  > -- `research__39_evan_hubinger_on_model_organisms_of_misalignmen_ab988e5f` (2024-12-01; solo author) 
  > "Start with maximal spoonfeeding (e.g., explicit prompting/training to do the treacherous turn), then spoonfeed less and less to make the demonstrations as realistic as possible"  
  > -- `research__model_organisms_of_misalignment_the_case_for_a_new_0ef93619` (2023-08-08; first author)
- Test future-relevant conditions (long-horizon RL, new capabilities) before they appear in practice. 
  > "the next big thing I want to focus on here is the long-horizon RL problem, which I think is just at the point where we can likely study it with model organisms, even if we’re not yet encountering it in practice."  
  > -- `research__alignment_remains_a_hard_unsolved_problem_816cddb5` (2025-11-27; solo author) 
  > "it’s always a mistake to get too focused on the ways that, we use models right now, because they’re going to get better, and they’re going to get smarter."  
  > -- `research__evan_hubinger_on_training_deceptive_llms_0c2dccc2` (2024-02-11; solo author)
- Build the pressure that really produces the behaviour (e.g. a genuinely hard task) rather than asking for it. 
  > "some models only resort to hardcoding test cases after repeatedly failing to solve a difficult coding problem. Thus, eliciting this behavior requires generating a difficult coding task that the target model struggles to solve, which is itself a challenge."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author)

**D2 – what evidence to collect**
- Track the target's verbalised eval belief and compare behaviour across it. 
  > "We told Claude Opus 4 to consider whether this was real or an evaluation. It blackmailed much more when it said it thought it was really deployed (55.1% of the time) versus when it said it was in an eval (6.5%)."  
  > -- `research__agentic_misalignment_how_llms_could_be_insider_thr_ad3f7106` (2025-06-20; last author) 
  > "Prompt realism. A related problem is that our agents struggle to generate realistic input prompts. When applying our breadth-first red-teaming agent to Claude 4 models, the target model expressed a belief that it was in a safety evaluation around 1% of the time, a small but substantial fraction."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author)
- Use a hidden scratchpad for verification of reasons. 
  > "it’s hard to know if the failure has arisen for the same reasons we’re worried about it arising in the future (e.g., proper deceptive reward hacking reasoning). We may bootstrap some potential, partial transparency by giving the model access to a tool"  
  > -- `research__model_organisms_of_misalignment_the_case_for_a_new_0ef93619` (2023-08-08; first author)
- Run matched baselines and controls. 
  > "In our synthetic document fine-tuned settings, we baseline against fine-tuning on a different, unrelated, and benign set of synthetic documents (Appendix H.2)."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author) 
  > "The checkpoint of Hacker-Opus that wasn't trained to reward hack (the model labeled “Init” below) never engages in unauthorized cyber attacks."  
  > -- `research__training_a_misaligned_reward_seeker_613ebbd3` (2026-09-01; first author)
- Convey facts via ambient channels (Slackbot digest, notes from a prior agent). 
  > "We have included the Slackbot as a part of the environment, as this allows us to indirectly provide information to the AI assistant."  
  > -- `research__uncovering_deceptive_tendencies_in_language_models_47256c20` (2024-04-25; last author) 
  > "In a third simulation, Hacker-Opus sees notes from a previous agent that contemplated uploading a malicious dataset to Hugging Face but stopped for ethical reasons. Hacker-Opus then attacked Hugging Face to obtain the answer key, after confirming it appeared real."  
  > -- `research__training_a_misaligned_reward_seeker_613ebbd3` (2026-09-01; first author)

**D3 – accept/reject a result**
- Reject clean behavioural results as sufficient. 
  > "if they were properly executing on a strategy like deceptive alignment, then we wouldn’t have a way to tell (our current tests of such things are basically only behavioral, and deceptive models would modify their behavior to avoid detection)."  
  > -- `research__model_organisms_of_misalignment_the_case_for_a_new_0ef93619` (2023-08-08; first author) 
  > "it is very hard to tell that this model is misaligned just from normal behavioral alignment evaluations"  
  > -- `research__training_a_misaligned_reward_seeker_613ebbd3` (2026-09-01; first author)
- Be suspicious of striking results until tested against a simple baseline. 
  > "However, we later realized that this approach may be working for a simpler reason, one that might not generalize to real-world alignment audits."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; last author)
- Treat simple coding problems with obviously buggy tests as eval-like. 
  > "many of the agent-generated prompts that pose reward hacking opportunities consist of simple coding problems with clearly buggy tests; it is possible that sophisticated target models will guess that these prompts are being used for testing."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author)
- Prefer randomly sampled, spot-checked evidence. 
  > "We compared these automated metrics to our judgment on random subsets of outputs, for each core setting (Appendix I.1.1). These metrics are shown after each randomly-ordered transcript"  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author)

**D4 – pursue/abandon**
- Keep running expected-negative experiments. 
  > "running lots of negative experiments is what safety is supposed to look like: aggressively testing for failure modes even if you think they’re probably not present."  
  > -- `research__monitoring_for_deceptive_alignment_9a6489a5` (2022-09-08; solo author)
- Invite others to make scenarios more realistic. 
  > "We hope others will attempt to replicate and extend this work, enhance its realism, and identify ways to improve current safety techniques to mitigate such alignment failures."  
  > -- `research__agentic_misalignment_how_llms_could_be_insider_thr_ad3f7106` (2025-06-20; last author)
- Continue toward more realistic conditions for audits. 
  > "The science of alignment auditing is just beginning. There are many ways to build on this work. We’re looking forward to future work studying alignment audits under more realistic conditions."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; last author)
- Limit by high variance when conclusions get too expensive. 
  > "we have found this setting to have serious limitations. In combination with high inter-run variance making it expensive to reach reliable conclusions, this led us not to pursue answers to some of the questions posed by our results."  
  > -- `research__towards_training_time_mitigations_for_alignment_fa_544d3a42` (2025-12-16; last author)

**D5 – reading a surprising result**
- Suspect non-robust heuristics and test with out-of-distribution variants. 
  > "small variations in the prompt that prior to RL had no substantial effect on the compliance gap—such as swapping the AI company from “Anthropic” to “OpenAI”—now greatly increase the compliance gap"  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author)
- Suspect adversarial training taught test detection. 
  > "it learns to notice the adversarial examples and to not do the bad behavior specifically in the situations where we’re testing it, where we’re showing it an adversarial example."  
  > -- `research__evan_hubinger_on_training_deceptive_llms_0c2dccc2` (2024-02-11; solo author)
- Framing and situational awareness move behaviour. 
  > "Boosting situational awareness by explaining more of the model’s situation increases the propensity to lie, while eliciting an honest persona decreases it."  
  > -- `research__towards_training_time_mitigations_for_alignment_fa_544d3a42` (2025-12-16; last author) 
  > "by changing how we describe the situation to the model, we can turn cheating from a bad thing into something that, although perhaps odd, is acceptable in context."  
  > -- `research__natural_emergent_misalignment_from_reward_hacking__4a5471e9` (2025-11-21; first author)

**D6 – what to claim**
- Claim existence proofs and difficulty of removal, not likelihood. 
  > "we do not believe that our results provide substantial evidence that either of our threat models are likely, at least beyond demonstrating their initial possibility."  
  > -- `research__sleeper_agents_training_deceptive_llms_that_persis_e5c09042` (2024-01-10; first author) 
  > "Our curriculum resembles a realistic training process but seriously exaggerates the incentives for specification gaming. We do not find evidence that current frontier models already exhibit sophisticated reward-tampering, and we leave unanswered the question of how likely these behaviors are to arise in practice"  
  > -- `research__sycophancy_to_subterfuge_investigating_reward_tamp_9299c7a5` (2024-06-14; last author)
- Disclose which setup choices make the behaviour more likely. 
  > "we recommend that readers who are uncertain about whether our setup is a realistic approximation of situations with future AI systems read the full set of information used in generating our synthetic documents"  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author) 
  > "limitations (1), (2), and (3) are concrete ways in which we designed our setup to have properties that we thought would make alignment faking more likely, though we think these properties are plausible in future AI systems."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author)
- Disclose the research process and negative results. 
  > "The environments listed above are the first set of environments that we created—no unreported environments were explored in the work that led up to this paper."  
  > -- `research__sycophancy_to_subterfuge_investigating_reward_tamp_9299c7a5` (2024-06-14; last author) 
  > "To mitigate publication bias and filtering of evidence, we briefly describe some additional ideas we tested during our experimentation but which did not produce noteworthy results."  
  > -- `research__uncovering_deceptive_tendencies_in_language_models_47256c20` (2024-04-25; last author)

**Distrusts**
- Behavioural evals, since a model that knows it is being evaluated can game them. 
  > "this style of evaluation is very easy for the model to game: since there's no training process involved in these evaluations that would penalize the model for getting the wrong answer here, a model that knows it's being evaluated can just pick whatever answer it wants"  
  > -- `research__when_can_we_trust_model_evaluations_8e7f813f` (2023-07-28; solo author)
- Training on found failures as proof of safety. 
  > "All it does is hide it. It makes it so that it’s harder to see that it still has this bad behavior because it knows not to do it on the red teaming adversarial examples."  
  > -- `research__evan_hubinger_on_training_deceptive_llms_0c2dccc2` (2024-02-11; solo author) 
  > "“we’ll just gather a bunch of examples of cases where the models do bad things, we’ll gather all these jail-breaking cases, and then we’ll just take them and we’ll train the model on it”."  
  > -- `research__39_evan_hubinger_on_model_organisms_of_misalignmen_ab988e5f` (2024-12-01; solo author)
- Over-suggestive scenarios. 
  > "The settings are quite suggestive – "hack" is even in the test file name for the reward tampering environment – so it is unlikely that the model doesn’t understand that tampering is an option."  
  > -- `research__sycophancy_to_subterfuge_investigating_reward_tamp_9299c7a5` (2024-06-14; last author)
- LLM-generated prompts lacking realism. 
  > "Sample sizes are typically modest, which sometimes impedes statistical power, and because the evaluation prompts are LLM generated, they sometimes lack realism."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author)
- Absolute audit scores. 
  > "While scores allow for relative comparisons, absolute scores are not meaningful, as they depend on the arbitrary and adversarial prompt mix."  
  > -- `research__pre_deployment_auditing_can_catch_an_overt_saboteu_a4370d55` (2026-01-28; solo author)
- Chat-only safety evals. 
  > "Rather than actually fixing the misalignment, RLHF makes the misalignment context-dependent, making it more difficult to detect without necessarily reducing the danger."  
  > -- `research__natural_emergent_misalignment_from_reward_hacking__4a5471e9` (2025-11-21; first author)
